choices.content: No; they depend on its magnitude and direction, not its placement
Yes; translating both endpoints changes its coordinates
The initial point must be placed at the origin

question.prompt: In a fixed coordinate system, do the coordinates of a fixed free vector depend on where its initial point is placed?

solutions.explanation: If the endpoints are \(A\) and \(B\), the vector is \(B-A\). Translating both endpoints by the same vector \(t\) gives \((B+t)-(A+t)=B-A\). Thus a fixed free vector has the same coordinates wherever it is placed. In fixed axes, its coordinates depend on both magnitude and direction. A is correct.
solutions.title: Translation cancellation
